title: 5e-4: HRR encoder + codebook + pipeline
description:
## Parent

sutra/83 (5e PRD: health metrics + similarity system)

## What to build

Port the HRR encoder from the spike (branch spike/hdc-ast-encoding, specifically hrr.rs) into a production similarity/ module. Compute strip + embed mode vectors for every function-level symbol at parse time.

- similarity/encoder.rs: recursive tree-structured encoding. For each function symbol's tree-sitter subtree: look up base vector for node kind from codebook, recursively encode children with position permutation (circular shift), bundle via elementwise average, bind with kind vector via circular convolution. Strip mode ignores identifier text; embed mode binds identifier names.
- similarity/codebook.rs: persistent random base vectors per AST node kind. Stored in durable partition (append-only, never modified). New entries created on first encounter.
- DB migration: hrr_vectors(symbol_id INTEGER, mode TEXT, vector BLOB) in ephemeral partition. hrr_codebook(key TEXT PK, vector BLOB) in durable partition.
- Pipeline integration: after tree-sitter symbol extraction, encode each function-level symbol into strip + embed vectors and store.
- Dimensions: 1024 f64s per vector (~8KB per vector, ~32MB for 2000-symbol workspace with two modes).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] similarity/encoder.rs ported from spike hrr.rs with strip + embed modes
- [ ] similarity/codebook.rs with durable SQLite storage, append-only semantics
- [ ] DB migration for hrr_vectors (ephemeral) and hrr_codebook (durable)
- [ ] Pipeline integration: HRR vectors computed at parse time for function-level symbols
- [ ] Vectors survive reparse (codebook stable → same input produces same vector)
- [ ] Tests: determinism (same tree → same vector), discrimination (different trees → different vectors), position sensitivity (reordered children → different vectors), strip ignores identifiers, embed distinguishes identifiers

## Blocked by

- sutra/87 (5e-review-1: checkpoint 1 quality gate)"
